title: A Casebook for Comparative Politics
description: This book is intended to serve as a companion text for courses in Comparative Politics, Introduction to Political Science, and similar subjects. The target audience is lower-division undergraduates. Each chapter constitutes a single country (case), with material on seven (7) major topics: History, Identity, Culture and Civil Society, Participation, Formal Institutions, Political Economy, and Foreign Relations.
authors: Mark L. Johnson - Author / Angela Pashayan - Author / Daniel I. Pedreira - Author / Matthew Schuster - Author / John Tures - Author / Cheryl Van Den Handel - Author / Helen Chang - Author / Petra Hendrickson - Author / Matthew Gritter - Author
